title: UNIT 4: FORCE, WORK, ENERGY AND POWER
notes:
✓ Force, work, energy and power → Describe why objects move and how energy is transferred.

✓ Dynamics → Branch of mechanics that studies motion and the forces causing it.

title: 4.1 THE CONCEPT OF FORCE
notes:
✓ Force → A push or pull that can change an object's motion, velocity, shape or size.

✓ Force → A vector quantity with magnitude and direction.

✓ SI unit → New­ton (N).

◆ TYPES OF FORCES
✓ Contact forces → Require physical contact.
✓ Non-contact forces → Act without physical contact.

✓ Contact examples → Applied, normal, friction and spring forces.
✓ Non-contact examples → Gravitational and magnetic forces.

title: 4.1.1 WEIGHT AND MEASURING FORCE
notes:
✓ Force → Can be measured using a spring balance; an applied force causes the spring to stretch and the scale gives the force value.

✓ Weight → Magnitude of the gravitational force acting on a body.

W = mg

✓ W → Weight.
✓ m → Mass.
✓ g → Acceleration due to gravity.

✓ SI unit of weight → Newton (N).

title: 4.2 NEWTON'S LAWS OF MOTION
notes:
✓ Newton's laws → Explain the relationship between force and motion.

◆ THREE LAWS
✓ First Law → Law of inertia.
✓ Second Law → Relationship between force and acceleration.
✓ Third Law → Action and reaction.

title: 4.2.1 NEWTON'S FIRST LAW — LAW OF INERTIA
notes:
✓ Newton's First Law → A body remains at rest or continues in uniform straight-line motion unless acted upon by an unbalanced external force.

✓ Inertia → Tendency of an object to resist a change in its state of motion.

✓ Greater mass → Greater inertia.

title: 4.2.2 NEWTON'S SECOND LAW
notes:
✓ Newton's Second Law → Acceleration of a body is directly proportional to the net force and inversely proportional to its mass.

F⃗ = m a⃗

✓ F → Net force.
✓ m → Mass.
✓ a → Acceleration.

✓ 1 N = 1 kg·m/s².

✓ Acceleration → Is in the direction of the net force.

title: 4.2.3 GRAVITY AND WEIGHT
notes:
✓ Gravitational force → Acts toward the center of Earth.

Fg = mg

✓ Near Earth's surface → g ≈ 9.8 m/s².

✓ Acceleration due to gravity → Changes with location; on the Moon it is about 1/6 of Earth's value.

✓ Mass → Measured in kg.
✓ Weight → A force measured in N.

title: 4.2.4 NEWTON'S THIRD LAW
notes:
✓ Newton's Third Law → For every action force, there is an equal and opposite reaction force.

F₁₂ = −F₂₁

◆ ACTION AND REACTION FORCES
✓ Equal magnitude.
✓ Opposite directions.
✓ Act on different objects.

✓ Forces → Always occur in pairs.

title: 4.3 FORCES OF FRICTION
notes:
✓ Friction → Force that resists the relative motion of two surfaces in contact.

✓ Friction → Is important for walking, running and the motion of wheeled vehicles.

✓ Friction → Depends on the normal force and the nature or roughness of the contacting surfaces.

✓ Rough surfaces → Generally produce greater friction than smooth surfaces.

title: 4.3.1 TYPES OF FRICTION
notes:
◆ STATIC FRICTION
✓ Static friction → Friction between surfaces when one body tends to slide over another but there is no sliding motion.

◆ KINETIC FRICTION
✓ Kinetic friction → Friction when one surface slides over another or when one body rolls over another.

✓ Static friction → Generally requires a larger force to overcome than kinetic friction.

title: 4.3.2 ADVANTAGES AND DISADVANTAGES OF FRICTION
notes:
◆ ADVANTAGES
✓ Allows us to walk and run.
✓ Provides grip between tires and roads.
✓ Helps vehicles stop.
✓ Allows objects to be held and moved safely.

◆ DISADVANTAGES
✓ Causes wear and tear.
✓ Produces unwanted heat.
✓ Opposes useful motion.
✓ Reduces mechanical efficiency.

title: 4.4 THE CONCEPT OF WORK
notes:
✓ Work → Is done when a force causes an object to move in the direction of the force.

W = F∥S

✓ W → Work.
✓ F∥ → Force parallel to displacement.
✓ S → Displacement.

✓ Work → Is a scalar quantity.

✓ SI unit → Joule (J).

✓ 1 J = 1 N·m.

✓ No work → Is done if there is no displacement or if the applied force has no component in the direction of displacement.

title: 4.5 KINETIC AND POTENTIAL ENERGIES
notes:
✓ Energy → Capacity to do work or cause change.

✓ Kinetic energy → Energy possessed by an object because of its motion.

Eₖ = ½mv²

✓ Potential energy → Energy possessed because of position or configuration.

◆ GRAVITATIONAL POTENTIAL ENERGY
Eₚ = mgh

✓ Mechanical energy → Kinetic energy + potential energy.

title: 4.6 POWER
notes:
✓ Power → Rate at which work is done or energy is transferred.

P = W/t = E/t

✓ P → Power.
✓ W → Work.
✓ E → Energy.
✓ t → Time.

✓ Power → Is a scalar quantity.

✓ SI unit → Watt (W).

✓ 1 W = 1 J/s.

✓ Same amount of work → The object or machine that does it in less time has greater power.

title: UNIT 4 — MUST REMEMBER
notes:
◆ FORCE
✓ Push or pull → Vector → N.

◆ WEIGHT
✓ Gravitational force → W = mg.

◆ NEWTON'S LAWS
✓ First Law → Inertia.
✓ Second Law → F = ma.
✓ Third Law → Equal and opposite action-reaction forces.

◆ FRICTION
✓ Friction → Opposes relative motion.
✓ Static friction → No sliding.
✓ Kinetic friction → Sliding or rolling motion.

◆ WORK
✓ W = F∥S → J.

◆ ENERGY
✓ Kinetic energy → Eₖ = ½mv².
✓ Potential energy → Eₚ = mgh.
✓ Mechanical energy → Eₖ + Eₚ.

◆ POWER
✓ P = W/t = E/t → W (watt).

◆ EXAM TIP
✓ Mass → kg.
✓ Weight → N.
✓ Force → Vector.
✓ Work, energy and power → Scalars.
